text: test suite lives tests/ — full docs tests/README.md. One case = one .R file tests/cases/; terminal runner human HTML report (tests/report.Rmd) execute files. Run package root: Visual cases (e.g. gs_*) save tests/output/<id>.png. console output emit also captured tests/output/<id>.txt diffed tests/expected/<id>.txt; snapshot, case must silent. Console cases (err_*, le_*) save tests/output/<id>.txt diffed automatically tests/expected/<id>.txt. gs_ case matching reference image tests/reference/ — ground-truth plot built independently geom_slice (plain ggplot2 + predict(), Applr, geom_smooth()). tests/reference/<id>.png correct geom_slice reproduce. Regenerate Rscript tests/reference/build_all.R (rarely needed — case’s data, model, styling changes).
code: Rscript tests/run.R            # all cases Rscript tests/run.R gs_14      # one case (prefix is enough) Rscript tests/run.R gs         # all geom_slice cases

title: CLAUDE.md — Developer Guide for Claude Code
text: Run case Rscript tests/run.R gs_XX FAILs — read message: either R error (find relevant source R/geom_slice.R, fix , re-run) console-output diff tests/expected/gs_XX_name.txt (decide whether code snapshot wrong) ’s NEW — case printed console output snapshot yet; read tests/output/gs_XX_name.txt, output correct intentional, accept Rscript tests/run.R --update gs_XX (never blanket-update) ’s OK — use Read tool view output (tests/output/gs_XX_name.png) reference (tests/reference/gs_XX_name.png) Compare output reference image (ground truth) # EXPECT: header top case file — line shape, slopes, per-group/per-facet positions, styling match reference plot looks wrong — fix source, re-run, re-view Move next case order (gs_01 → gs_02 → … → gs_18) complete, run Rscript -e "rmarkdown::render('tests/report.Rmd')" human review work OK runner means case ran, produced plot, console output () matched snapshot — step 4’s visual comparison decides plot correctness. editing adding cases, follow case-file anatomy tests/README.md (structured # CASE: / # TYPE: / # FUNC: / # EXPECT: header, source("tests/_setup.R") first, ggsave() — runner renders).

what: Fit a model, then autoplot() it
title: Getting started with Applr
text: Start model mpg depends two predictors: autoplot() quickest way see . rebuilds scatterplot model’s data, picks first numeric predictor x-axis, adds slice line — subtitle recording values predictors held :  message tells happened: hp axis, line holds mean. Use x_axis slice along different predictor, pass geom_slice() argument ...:
code: model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars) lm_equation(model) #> [1] "mpg = 30.7 - 0.0303*disp - 0.0248*hp" autoplot(model) #> Value for `hp` not specified - Used mean: 146.7 #>     To choose a slice, use 'predict_vars = list(hp = 146.7)'. autoplot(model, x_axis = "hp", interval = "confidence") #> Value for `disp` not specified - Used mean: 230.7 #>     To choose a slice, use 'predict_vars = list(disp = 230.7)'.

code: model_cyl <- lm(mpg ~ disp * cyl, data = mtcars)  ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = disp, y = mpg, color = factor(cyl))) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model_cyl)

what: geom_slice() — your model as a ggplot2 layer
title: Visualize and Explain Linear Models
text: geom_slice() draws prediction line fitted lm() across plot (facets). looks like geom_smooth(), geom_smooth() fits model plotted data, geom_slice() draws model fitted. predictor x-axis varies along line; every predictor fixed, creating 2d “slice” high-dimensional model. Variables named predict_vars held chosen values. Variables mapped grouping aesthetic (aes(color = g)) pinned group’s value — one line per group. Facet variables pinned panel’s value. Anything left imputed (mean numeric, common value factors), console message naming value used.
code: library(ggplot2) model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp + cyl, data = mtcars)  ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   facet_wrap(~cyl) +   geom_slice(model, predict_vars = list(hp = 110),              color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1)

what: autoplot() — a complete plot in one call
title: Visualize and Explain Linear Models
text: autoplot() lm builds whole plot: model’s data scatter geom_slice() line . model’s first numeric predictor goes x-axis (override x_axis), everything ... passed geom_slice(). result regular ggplot, extend + usual.  data mapping go ggplot() : pass model’s data extra columns aesthetics, override add automatic aes() (entries named x y replace chosen axes).   (static snapshot — real plot interactive: drag rotate, hover values) Note: model must fitted data argument (lm(y ~ x, data = your_data)) autoplot() can recover data.
code: library(ggplot2)   # for labs() below; autoplot() itself needs only Applr  autoplot(lm(mpg ~ disp, data = mtcars))  # Pass geom_slice() options through; the result is a normal ggplot autoplot(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars),          predict_vars = list(hp = 110), interval = "confidence") +   labs(title = "Slice at hp = 110") # Choose the x-axis autoplot(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars), x_axis = "hp") cars2 <- transform(mtcars, cyl_f = factor(cyl)) autoplot(lm(mpg ~ disp, data = mtcars),          data = cars2, mapping = aes(color = cyl_f)) # Two numeric predictors? Get the interactive 3-D surface instead autoplot(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars), type = "3d")

title: Visualize and Explain Linear Models
text: Create new base-R plot showing 2-D slice linear model. Unspecified x_axis defaults first variable model; unspecified predictor values held sensible defaults (numeric → mean, factor → first level) reported caption.
code: model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars) slice_2d(model) #--or-- slice_2d(model, x_axis = "hp", disp = 250, n = 150, col = "blue", lwd = 2)

title: Visualize and Explain Linear Models
text: Add 2-D slice line existing base-R plot. X Y axis variables must match plot added .  example work Y axes match (y 1/y):
code: model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars) plot(mpg ~ disp, data = mtcars) add_slice_2d(model)  # Multiple slices on one plot model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars) plot(mpg ~ disp, data = mtcars) add_slice_2d(model, hp = min(mtcars$hp), col = "blue") add_slice_2d(model, hp = max(mtcars$hp), col = "red", lty = 2) model <- lm(1/mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars) plot(mpg ~ disp, data = mtcars) add_slice_2d(model) # will not plot

title: Visualize and Explain Linear Models
text: Create interactive 3-D scatter plot fitted regression surface (models must exactly two numeric predictors). Points colored response along colors gradient, transformed terms (x^2) graph raw predictors. also reachable autoplot(model, type = "3d").  (static snapshot — real plot interactive: drag rotate, hover values)
code: model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars) scatter_3d(model, colors = c("blue", "yellow")) # Transformed terms graph over their raw predictors scatter_3d(lm(mpg ~ wt + I(wt^2) + hp, data = mtcars))

title: Visualize and Explain Linear Models
text: Return fitted model’s equation plain text, print LaTeX-formatted (ideal LaTeX R Markdown documents). clearer = TRUE spells factor terms readably.
code: model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars) lm_equation(model) #> [1] "mpg = 30.7 - 0.0303*disp - 0.0248*hp" lm_latex(model) #> $$\underbrace{\hat{Y_i}}_{\text{Pred. mpg}} = 30.7 - 0.0303\underbrace{X_{1i}}_{\text{disp}} - 0.0248\underbrace{X_{2i}}_{\text{hp}}$$

title: Visualize and Explain Linear Models
text: Low-level ggproto objects power geom_slice(). users never need call directly, can custom layers. Note StatSlice reads aesthetic mapping params — geom_slice() supplies automatically, raw layer() call must pass explicitly:
code: library(ggplot2) model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp + cyl, data = mtcars)  ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   layer(stat = StatSlice,         geom = GeomSlice,         position = "identity",         inherit.aes = TRUE,         params = list(model = model, predict_vars = list(hp = 110),                       mapping = aes(disp, mpg)))

title: Visualize and Explain Linear Models
text: • multi-variable models, use predict_vars (e.g. list(hp = 110)) choose slice want. • Factors included facet_wrap() facet_grid() also appear model pass geom_slice(). • New R modeling? lm(y ~ x1 + x2, data = df) fits linear model y x1 x2.

title: Visualize and Explain Linear Models
text: • Use R’s built-help: ?geom_slice, ?autoplot.lm, ?slice_2d, ?scatter_3d, etc. • Found bug suggestion? Open issue https://github.com/saundersg/Applr/issues. Enjoy clearer model visualizations Applr!

text: object linear model fitted lm() data argument — data recovered model, lm(y ~ x, data = your_data) works lm(your_data$y ~ your_data$x) . ... Passed geom_slice() — example predict_vars = list(hp = 110) choose slice, interval = "confidence" ribbon, fixed aesthetics color = "red" — scatter_3d() type = "3d". data data frame draw scatter instead data recovered model — example model's data extra columns added mapping aesthetics. Passed ggplot2::ggplot(). rows must still match data model fitted (geom_slice() checks, errors mismatch). mapping Extra aesthetics created ggplot2::aes(), passed ggplot2::ggplot() — example mapping = aes(color = factor(cyl)). Entries named x y override automatically chosen axes. type "2d" (default) geom_slice() ggplot, "3d" interactive scatter_3d() surface (needs exactly two numeric predictors). x_axis name predictor place x-axis, x_axis = "disp". Defaults model's first numeric predictor. Ignored type = "3d". xaxis Deprecated; use x_axis instead.

text: Pass type = "3d" model exactly two numeric predictors get interactive scatter_3d() surface instead 2-D slice; ... forwarded scatter_3d() (e.g. n, colors). model's first numeric predictor goes x-axis (override x_axis) raw response variable goes y-axis. Everything else handled geom_slice() reported console: predictors visible plot imputed (mean numeric, common value factor/character), transformed response lm(log(y) ~ x) automatically back-transformed match raw y-axis.

title: Automatically plot a linear model — autoplot.lm
code: library(ggplot2)  # A complete plot from a model in one call autoplot(lm(mpg ~ disp, data = mtcars))   # Predictors not on the plot are imputed (a message says how) autoplot(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars)) #> Value for `hp` not specified - Used mean: 146.7 #>     To choose a slice, use 'predict_vars = list(hp = 146.7)'.   # Choose which predictor goes on the x-axis autoplot(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars), x_axis = "hp") #> Value for `disp` not specified - Used mean: 230.7 #>     To choose a slice, use 'predict_vars = list(disp = 230.7)'.   # Transformed response, back-transformed onto the raw mpg axis autoplot(lm(log(mpg) ~ disp, data = mtcars)) #> Predictions of `log(mpg)` were back-transformed to match the `mpg` axis. #>     To turn this off, use 'back_transform = FALSE'.   # Options pass through to geom_slice(); the result is a normal ggplot autoplot(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars),          predict_vars = list(hp = 110), interval = "confidence") +   labs(title = "Slice at hp = 110")   # Custom data and extra aesthetics for the scatter autoplot(lm(mpg ~ disp, data = mtcars),          data = mtcars, mapping = aes(color = factor(cyl)))   # An interactive 3-D surface for a two-predictor model if (interactive()) {   autoplot(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars), type = "3d") }

title: Display a 2D slice of a linear model — geom_slice
code: library(ggplot2)  # Basic use, like geom_smooth() but drawing *your* model. hp is not on # the plot, so it is held at its mean (a console message says so). model <- lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars) ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model) #> Value for `hp` not specified - Used mean: 146.7 #>     To choose a slice, use 'predict_vars = list(hp = 146.7)'.   # Choose the slice yourself ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model, predict_vars = list(hp = 110))   # Several values draw one line per value (label them with # geom_slice_text()); several multi-value variables are crossed ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model, predict_vars = list(hp = c(66, 150, 335)))   # Confidence or prediction ribbon around the line ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model, predict_vars = list(hp = 110), interval = "confidence")   # A grouping aesthetic pins its predictor to each group's own value: # one line per cylinder count, each with its own slope model2 <- lm(mpg ~ disp * cyl, data = mtcars) ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg, color = factor(cyl))) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model2)   # full_range = TRUE extends each group's line across the whole panel, # not just its own data range ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg, color = factor(cyl))) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model2, full_range = TRUE)   # Facet variables pin per panel the same way ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model2) +   facet_wrap(~ cyl)   # A transformed response is back-transformed automatically: the model # predicts log(mpg), the line appears in raw mpg units (a message says so) model3 <- lm(log(mpg) ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars) ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model3) #> Value for `hp` not specified - Used mean: 146.7 #>     To choose a slice, use 'predict_vars = list(hp = 146.7)'. #> Predictions of `log(mpg)` were back-transformed to match the `mpg` axis. #>     To turn this off, use 'back_transform = FALSE'.   # ... or control the mapping yourself with back_transform ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model3, back_transform = exp) #> Value for `hp` not specified - Used mean: 146.7 #>     To choose a slice, use 'predict_vars = list(hp = 146.7)'.   # A projection band spanning hp between two values, instead of a line ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model, predict_vars = list(hp = c(66, 335)), band = "hp")   # n controls how many prediction points make up the line ggplot(mtcars, aes(disp, mpg)) +   geom_point() +   geom_slice(model, predict_vars = list(hp = 110), n = 10)

title: Write out the equation of a linear model — lm_equation
code: # Simple regression lm_equation(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)) #> [1] "mpg = 37.3 - 5.34*wt"  # Multiple predictors lm_equation(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp, data = mtcars)) #> [1] "mpg = 30.7 - 0.0303*disp - 0.0248*hp"  # Factor predictor: one term per non-reference level model <- lm(Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width + Species, data = iris) lm_equation(model) #> [1] "Sepal.Length = 2.25 + 0.804*Sepal.Width + 1.46*Speciesversicolor + 1.95*Speciesvirginica"  # `clearer = TRUE` spells out factor levels lm_equation(model, clearer = TRUE) #> [1] "Sepal.Length = 2.25 + 0.804*Sepal.Width + 1.46*(Species=\"versicolor\") + 1.95*(Species=\"virginica\")"  # Transformed terms and interactions lm_equation(lm(mpg ~ wt + I(wt^2), data = mtcars)) #> [1] "mpg = 49.9 - 13.4*wt + 1.17*I(wt^2)" lm_equation(lm(Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width * Species, data = iris)) #> [1] "Sepal.Length = 2.64 + 0.69*Sepal.Width + 0.901*Speciesversicolor + 1.27*Speciesvirginica + 0.175*Sepal.Width:Speciesversicolor + 0.211*Sepal.Width:Speciesvirginica"  # No-intercept models print no intercept lm_equation(lm(mpg ~ 0 + wt, data = mtcars)) #> [1] "mpg = 5.29*wt"

code: # Simple regression lm_latex(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)) #> $$\underbrace{\hat{Y_i}}_{\text{Pred. mpg}} = 37.3 - 5.34\underbrace{X_{1i}}_{\text{wt}}$$  # Multiple predictors and a transformed term lm_latex(lm(mpg ~ disp + hp + I(hp^2), data = mtcars)) #> $$\underbrace{\hat{Y_i}}_{\text{Pred. mpg}} = 37.4 - 0.0189\underbrace{X_{1i}}_{\text{disp}} - 0.138\underbrace{X_{2i}}_{\text{hp}} + 0.00028\underbrace{X_{3i}}_{\text{I(hp^2)}}$$  # Factor predictor with interactions; `clearer = TRUE` spells out levels model <- lm(Sepal.Length ~ Sepal.Width * Species, data = iris) lm_latex(model, clearer = TRUE) #> $$\underbrace{\hat{Y_i}}_{\text{Pred. Sepal.Length}} = 2.64 + 0.69\underbrace{X_{1i}}_{\text{Sepal.Width}} + 0.901\underbrace{X_{2i}}_{\text{(Species="versicolor")}} + 1.27\underbrace{X_{3i}}_{\text{(Species="virginica")}} + 0.175\underbrace{X_{4i}}_{\text{Sepal.Width:(Species="versicolor")}} + 0.211\underbrace{X_{5i}}_{\text{Sepal.Width:(Species="virginica")}}$$  # Capture the string instead of just printing it eq <- lm_latex(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)) #> $$\underbrace{\hat{Y_i}}_{\text{Pred. mpg}} = 37.3 - 5.34\underbrace{X_{1i}}_{\text{wt}}$$ nchar(eq) #> [1] 90
